purpose: General Solo progression at comparable permanent investment, including access to the 400-coin Starting move upgrade. Current move rules and player discussions inform editorial grades; saved leaderboard results predate this patch. No controlled playtests claimed.

picks.reason: Mewtwo remains one of our first picks. Players repeatedly recommend it, its Psychic moves receive the single-type bonus, and the saved weekly board contains nine Mewtwo records.
picks.watchFor: We'd pair Special damage with Nasty Plot, not Swords Dance. The new Psychic control moves give you options, but don't assume every slot attacks before you earn Bonds.

picks.reason: We keep Gengar in S because player recommendations, a clear Ghost/Poison plan and ten saved weekly records point in the same direction. Poison or slow can set up stronger Hex hits.
picks.watchFor: We'd use Nasty Plot for Special damage. Poison and Hex need to share an active Bond group to keep firing together; merely owning both isn't the full setup.

picks.reason: Eternatus stays high on our list for Sludge and the expanded Poison/Dragon pool. Its HP and speed give you room to build around status and damage.
picks.watchFor: We keep it in A while the new routes settle. It doesn't receive the single-type bonus, and older complaints about giant collision size should not be carried over unchanged.

picks.reason: We rate Giratina as a strong A option for its HP and Ghost/Dragon choices. Dragon Breath can apply slow for Hex once you can keep the relevant attacks running together.
picks.watchFor: We'd take a coherent damage route as well as defensive cards. The old saved records support viability, not a confirmed best build for this patch.

picks.reason: We like Palkia's Special Water/Dragon options, with Aqua Ring for regeneration and Whirlpool or Dragon Breath for another way to manage enemies. Water Gun remains a useful default.
picks.watchFor: We keep it in A rather than calling it a proven top pick. The saved all-time board has only one Palkia record, and it predates the expanded move pool.

picks.reason: We like Tentacruel for a Water/Poison plan that includes Aqua Ring, poison and the new Whirlpool control option. It also appears five times in the saved weekly Solo board.
picks.watchFor: We'd secure healing and a workable main attack before chasing extra moves. Shell Bell is capped at 4 HP per second; poison isn't unlimited sustain.

picks.reason: We'd lean into Sludge first: it already uses Munkidori's 1.42 Special attack. Psychic moves give you another direction if the cards suit it.
picks.watchFor: Watch the 66 physical defense. When you change attacks, remember that the other moves in your slots aren't all firing alongside it.

picks.reason: Appletun is our slower Grass/Dragon alternative, with Vine Whip, new ranged Grass options and Dragon Dance for a Physical plan. Its 45:00 saved result is worth noting.
picks.watchFor: We wouldn't call it strongest from that result alone. Move early at speed 91, and don't mistake Grass Knot or an evolution name for guaranteed healing.

picks.reason: We put Slaking among our first picks for a Physical Normal plan. Its own-type damage bonus, active melee reduction and 138 HP support Tackle or Body Slam; the saved weekly board also includes a 35:02 run.
picks.watchFor: We'd build a usable damage group before chasing more buffs. Normal has no super-effective matchups, and the saved result is from before this patch.

picks.reason: Marshadow is one of our stronger melee choices. Karate Chop fits its 1.39 Physical attack, and speed 130 helps you choose when to get close.
picks.watchFor: Keep a way out after each approach. If you switch to Special Ghost damage, you're also switching to its lower attack factor.

picks.reason: We'd consider Zapdos when we want the Electric projectile start with Flying moves available as another option. Thunder Shock uses 1.39 Special attack.
picks.watchFor: Change how you move when you change attacks. Discharge needs you closer to enemies than Thunder Shock does.

picks.reason: Alakazam gets our vote if you're happy to trade safety for a strong ranged opening. Homing Confusion uses 1.44 Special attack, with speed 128 for repositioning.
picks.watchFor: Don't let the damage tempt you into standing still. Its 95 HP and 45 physical defense leave very little room for contact.

picks.reason: We like Jolteon for a mobile Electric start: Thunder Shock gives you piercing shots, and speed 133 helps keep a gap open.
picks.watchFor: We'd take the defensive weakness seriously. It has 99 HP and 60 physical defense, with less type variety than some alternatives.

picks.reason: Mew is our more balanced alternative to the fragile Psychic picks. You still open with Confusion, but have 115 HP and both defenses at 100.
picks.watchFor: Expect less damage from its 1.25 Special attack than Mewtwo's. Choose from the moves actually in its pool rather than planning around its main-game reputation.

picks.reason: We'd pick Espeon for a focused Special Psychic plan. Confusion homes in and uses its 1.42 Special attack from the start.
picks.watchFor: Protect the gap around you: 99 HP and 60 physical defense aren't much of a cushion. Psycho Cut uses its weaker Physical side.

picks.reason: Raikou makes our A tier as a balanced Electric option. Thunder Shock fits its stronger attack side, with speed 126 and 110 HP behind it.
picks.watchFor: Physical defense is the weaker side at 75. Choose between Thunderbolt and Discharge based on how close you want to play.

picks.reason: We'd build Tyranitar around Physical Rock damage first. Rock Throw fits 1.44 Physical attack, with 115 HP and strong defenses behind it.
picks.watchFor: Move early with speed 104. If you take a Dark move, check its attack category before spending on buffs.

picks.reason: We like Ho-Oh when Special hits are your main concern: 118 HP and 154 Special defense give you a substantial buffer, with Fire and Flying options.
picks.watchFor: Ember uses 1.31 Special attack, not the higher Physical factor. That huge Special defense doesn't apply to Physical hits.

picks.reason: Celebi appeals to us as a balanced Confusion starter with Grass options when you want a change of attack pattern.
picks.watchFor: Check the category before changing your buffs. Grass Knot is area damage; don't choose it expecting to recover HP.

picks.reason: We'd lean into Metal Claw on Metagross. Its 1.44 Physical attack and 130 physical defense support that opening, with Psychic moves available later.
picks.watchFor: Plan exits before you need them; speed 107 isn't especially high. Confusion uses its lower Special attack.

picks.reason: We like Groudon for a Physical Ground plan with Bonemerang, Magnitude or other area options. Ground attacks benefit from its single-type bonus.
picks.watchFor: Mud Shot is still the default and uses the lower Special factor. Buying Starting move can remove that mismatch; take the opening you intend to support.

picks.reason: We like Jirachi as a balanced Metal Claw starter. Active melee reduction sits alongside 115 HP and both defenses at 100.
picks.watchFor: Keep upgrading damage. Neither attack factor exceeds 1.25, so we'd avoid spending every choice on defense.

picks.reason: We'd consider Lucario if you want both a Physical melee route and a viable Special alternative. Karate Chop fits Physical attack; Aura Sphere uses 1.33 Special attack.
picks.watchFor: Choose your distance deliberately. With 102 HP and both defenses at 70, getting trapped still hurts despite melee reduction.

picks.reason: Magnezone is our sturdier Physical-defense option for a Special Electric start. Thunder Shock uses 1.42 Special attack, with 115 physical defense.
picks.watchFor: Speed 103 calls for early repositioning. Metal Claw may be available, but it uses the weaker Physical factor.

picks.reason: We'd use Dialga's Steel and Dragon choices to build around the attack side we want. Starting move lets you choose a Special opening to use its stronger factor.
picks.watchFor: Metal Claw remains the default, not a requirement after the unlock. We'd check the category of the chosen start before spending on attack buffs.

picks.reason: We like Manaphy's straightforward Water choices: Water Gun to start, slowing Bubble attacks and Aqua Ring if you want regeneration.
picks.watchFor: Its 1.25 Special attack trails Palkia's. We'd keep taking damage upgrades rather than expecting regeneration to carry the run.

picks.reason: Darkrai's rating should reflect the Starting move upgrade: we'd consider a Special Dark opening instead of judging every run by default Bite. Its own-type attacks now get the single-type bonus.
picks.watchFor: The complaint about its Bite opening is real, but comes from an older version. Choose a legal starting attack after buying the upgrade rather than treating that weakness as permanent.

picks.reason: Victini is one of our flexible Confusion starters. Fire adds burn and different attack patterns without a major defensive weak side in its base stats.
picks.watchFor: We'd stick with one main attack early. Taking a new move at every opportunity can leave the whole set short on levels.

picks.reason: We like Chandelure's own Fire/Ghost options for setting up Hex. Shadow Ball already uses a strong 1.50 Special factor at the start.
picks.watchFor: Apply burn before expecting the stronger Hex hits. With 97 HP and speed 112, leave yourself time to get out.

picks.reason: Thundurus gives us a fast Electric opening with Flying choices later. Thunder Shock lines up with its 1.39 Special attack and speed 125.
picks.watchFor: Don't drift into contact while picking cards. Its 70 physical defense makes repeated hits costly.

picks.reason: We'd start Reshiram around Dragon Rage, which already uses its 1.52 Special attack. Fire gives you another direction when the upgrades arrive.
picks.watchFor: Fire isn't your starting move. Keep weather and enemy types in mind when deciding which attack to use.

picks.reason: Keldeo is an easy pick for our ranged shortlist: Water Gun and Aura Sphere both use its stronger Special side, with Aqua Ring available too.
picks.watchFor: We'd think twice before switching to Karate Chop without a plan. It uses only 1.10 Physical attack.

picks.reason: We like Greninja for keeping a Water Gun gap open at speed 129. Water and Dark offer several ways to change your attack pattern later.
picks.watchFor: Avoid narrow escape routes. With defenses of 67 and 71, the cost of getting surrounded is high.

picks.reason: Hoopa makes our A tier on the strength of homing Confusion at 1.52 Special attack, with Ghost attacks available as alternatives.
picks.watchFor: Give yourself an exit before approaching a crowd. Speed 107 and 60 physical defense make late escapes risky.

picks.reason: We like Lunala if you want a homing Psychic start with more HP behind it. Its 132 HP and 1.45 Special attack are a useful combination.
picks.watchFor: We'd finish a promising main attack before chasing every Psychic and Ghost option. You don't get all their damage at once.

picks.reason: Xurkitree is our pick when Electric damage is the priority. Thunder Shock uses its 1.65 Special attack immediately.
picks.watchFor: We wouldn't choose it for safety alone. Speed 113 and both defenses at 71 still require careful movement.

picks.reason: We rate Blacephalon for its Special damage and Fire/Ghost choices. Ember uses 1.53 Special attack, and burn can help set up Hex later.
picks.watchFor: Treat it as a fragile attacker. With 94 HP and 53 physical defense, we'd keep space rather than trade hits.

picks.reason: We like Zeraora for the room speed 138 gives you around a Thunder Shock opening. Its 110 HP is useful, too.
picks.watchFor: Build for the move you're using. Thunder Shock takes the 1.26 Special factor, not its higher Physical factor.

picks.reason: We'd choose Sneasler for a fast Karate Chop plan. Speed 128 and 1.42 Physical attack fit that job, with Poison alternatives available.
picks.watchFor: Melee reduction helps, but 60 physical defense remains a weakness. Special attacks use only a 0.92 factor.

picks.reason: Skeledirge gets our A tier for a Fire opening backed by 117 HP and 100 physical defense, with Ghost options for later choices.
picks.watchFor: Start leaving a closing gap early at speed 106. If you choose Hex, make sure you have a way to apply status first.

picks.reason: We like Flutter Mane for fast ranged damage: Shadow Ball uses 1.44 Special attack, and speed 135 helps you keep moving.
picks.watchFor: Its 135 Special defense can hide a very different Physical weakness. With 95 HP and 55 physical defense, contact is dangerous.
picks.name: Flutter Mane

picks.reason: We'd build Iron Moth around its stronger Special side. Ember uses 1.47, with Fire and Poison options for status and different attack patterns.
picks.watchFor: Keep out of contact with that 60 physical defense. We'd upgrade a main attack before spreading levels across both types.
picks.name: Iron Moth

picks.reason: We rate Gholdengo for a planned Special Ghost/Steel route. The Starting move upgrade lets you begin with a legal attack that fits its stronger Special factor.
picks.watchFor: Without that unlock, Metal Claw still opens on only 1.03 Physical attack. We'd account for the actual save rather than assuming every player starts fully configured.

picks.reason: We like Iron Valiant's choice between Physical and Special routes. Both factors are useful, and speed 127 helps you reposition.
picks.watchFor: You start with Fairy Wind. Build for that until you actually change routes, and watch the lower Special defense of 60.
picks.name: Iron Valiant

picks.reason: We'd consider Venusaur for a Vine Whip start with Grass area attacks and Poison choices to build toward. Its 106 HP gives you something to work with.
picks.watchFor: We put it below the leading ranged starters because its damage factors are more modest. Pick a main route instead of taking every type option.

picks.reason: Charizard has plenty we'd want to build around: Ember uses 1.30 Special attack, with Fire and Flying attacks to choose from later.
picks.watchFor: Give the opening move some levels before branching out. We'd check attack categories rather than automatically stacking Physical buffs.

picks.reason: Raichu is a straightforward Electric choice if that's what you have unlocked. Thunder Shock gives piercing shots and familiar follow-up options.
picks.watchFor: At equal investment we'd lean toward Jolteon or Raikou. Raichu's 55 physical defense and 1.20 Special attack are the trade-off.

picks.reason: We'd start Nidoking with Sludge and then decide whether to stay with Special damage or move toward Physical Bonemerang.
picks.watchFor: Make that decision before taking attack buffs. Sludge uses 1.17 Special attack, not Nidoking's higher Physical factor.

picks.reason: Golduck gives us a simple Water plan: piercing Water Gun, slowing Bubble attacks and Aqua Ring for regeneration.
picks.watchFor: We'd choose the stronger Water alternatives at equal investment. Its 1.22 Special factor and moderate bulk keep it in B for us.

picks.reason: We'd build Hitmonlee around Karate Chop and its 1.36 Physical attack. Active melee reduction and 110 Special defense help justify getting close.
picks.watchFor: Be careful with contact: 92 HP and 53 physical defense are thin. Aura Sphere uses only 0.89 Special attack.

picks.reason: We like Crobat's speed 133 for repositioning. Sludge starts at range, with Flying moves available if you want another attack pattern.
picks.watchFor: The opening damage is the reason we keep it in B: Sludge uses only 1.08 Special attack.

picks.reason: Porygon2 is a reasonable Normal choice when you want fairly balanced defenses. Its 108 HP gives the opening some room.
picks.watchFor: We'd plan beyond Tackle, which uses 1.14 Physical attack rather than its stronger Special side. The typed move pool is narrow.

picks.reason: Blaziken offers Fire and Fighting routes with both attack factors above 1.30. We'd choose the attack style first, then support it with upgrades.
picks.watchFor: Ember doesn't grant melee reduction. Speed 112 and both defenses at 70 mean you still need to protect your opening.

picks.reason: We'd use Aggron's 180 physical defense to support Metal Claw and a Physical damage plan.
picks.watchFor: Don't mistake that number for protection against everything. Speed 99 and 60 Special defense are why we keep it below the more rounded picks.

picks.reason: Regirock is worth considering when Physical hits are your concern. Rock Throw starts on a 106-HP partner with 200 physical defense.
picks.watchFor: We'd plan escape routes early at speed 99. Its damage and narrower typed pool are the compromises.

picks.reason: We move Deoxys to A for a fast Special Psychic plan. Its single-type bonus and new homing or pushback options make its damage and speed easier to build around.
picks.watchFor: 92 HP still leaves less room for errors. Speed above 130 has reduced extra value during Judgment, so we'd also invest in damage control and survival.

picks.reason: We'd consider Infernape when you want Fire and Fighting choices without a huge gap between its attack factors. Speed 123 helps.
picks.watchFor: Its defenses are only 71 on both sides. If you switch into melee, change how you position as well as which buffs you take.

picks.reason: Rampardos moves into our A choices for Physical Rock damage. It benefits from the single-type bonus, and Rock Tomb adds a control option to its expanded pool.
picks.watchFor: We'd protect its slower turns at speed 102. Its Rock attacks still have matchups to work around; high damage isn't a reason to walk into marked zones.

picks.reason: Spiritomb gives us a ranged Shadow Ball start with both defenses at 108. Ghost and Dark leave a few directions open.
picks.watchFor: Move before you need to at speed 93. Its 92 HP isn't a large reserve, and Hex needs status on the target.

picks.reason: Gallade is a B pick we'd take with a Physical route in mind, using Psycho Cut or Fighting options rather than committing Special buffs to default Confusion.
picks.watchFor: Starting move can fix the opening mismatch. We'd still check what attacks are actually active together before choosing between damage, control and defense.

picks.reason: Whimsicott is worth a look if you want a faster Vine Whip option. Speed 127 helps you choose your distance, with Grass and Fairy choices later.
picks.watchFor: We'd prioritize damage early: its attack factors are only 1.07/1.12. Grass attacks here aren't a team-healing kit.

picks.reason: We'd start Archeops with a Physical Rock plan. Speed 124 and 1.47 Physical attack fit Rock Throw well.
picks.watchFor: Both defenses are 65, so we'd keep moving instead of trading hits. Its damage stats don't make it a safe default.

picks.reason: Cobalion gives us a fast Metal Claw option with 111 HP and 129 physical defense, plus active melee reduction.
picks.watchFor: Its damage factors are only 1.20 on both sides. We'd keep taking damage upgrades while watching the lower Special defense of 72.

picks.reason: We like Delphox's option to move from Ember into Psychic attacks. Its 1.33 Special factor supports either direction.
picks.watchFor: We'd choose one main attack early. Splitting upgrades across both types can leave you short on damage, and physical defense is only 72.

picks.reason: We move Kartana up for its Physical Grass/Steel choices, including Vine Whip and Metal Claw. The expanded pool gives you more ways to control space around a melee plan.
picks.watchFor: We wouldn't dismiss it just for 31 Special defense: the defense penalty is capped. Fire matchups and your positioning matter more than reading that number like a main-series stat.

picks.reason: We'd build Cinderace around Physical Fire damage such as Flame Charge or Flame Wheel. The single-type bonus and a selectable opening give that route a clearer start.
picks.watchFor: Default Ember uses only 1.06 Special attack. Buy the opening upgrade if changing routes; Physical buffs won't fix Ember on their own.

picks.reason: Toxtricity offers us a Special Electric start with Poison options later. Thunder Shock already uses its 1.33 factor.
picks.watchFor: Speed 110 and defenses of 70 make it less forgiving than the faster Electric picks. We'd leave extra room to turn away.

picks.reason: We like Dragapult's speed 138 for keeping clear space around Dragon Rage. Ghost gives you another route later.
picks.watchFor: Dragon Rage uses 1.25 Special attack, not its higher Physical factor. We'd choose upgrades for the attack actually on screen.

picks.reason: We'd consider Ceruledge for Physical Fire/Ghost choices such as Flame Charge or Shadow Sneak, with a matching opening after buying Starting move.
picks.watchFor: Default Ember uses its lower Special factor. The revised pool offers alternatives, but we wouldn't assume healing just from its main-game identity.

picks.reason: Tatsugiri gives us a Special Dragon start with useful Water choices later: piercing shots, slow and Aqua Ring.
picks.watchFor: We'd keep contact to a minimum with 101 HP and 60 physical defense. Plan around the moves here rather than a presumed Dondozo pairing.

picks.reason: Voltorb offers a mobile Electric start with piercing Thunder Shock, and now has Thunder Wave and bouncing Electro Ball as additional choices.
picks.watchFor: We'd choose another reviewed Electric partner at equal investment. Its lower damage and HP remain trade-offs even though the single-type bonus also benefits it.

picks.reason: Chansey belongs in B for us, not automatically at the bottom. Its 182 HP is meaningful under the softened defense rule, and Normal moves now get the single-type bonus.
picks.watchFor: We'd plan for damage first, potentially using a Special Normal opening after buying Starting move. Low attack still slows clearing; it isn't a team-healing kit.

picks.reason: Magcargo still offers Fire and Rock area/control choices, including the expanded Rock pool, if you want to make the slower approach work.
picks.watchFor: We'd take a faster option for general Solo progression. Speed 91 and awkward Water/Ground matchups are the larger concerns; high Physical defense alone won't solve them.
